# OSINT Methodology

> Copy of [OSINT Methodology](https://github.com/SOsintOps/intelligence-field-notes/blob/main/docs/osint-methodology.md) from [Intelligence Field Notes](https://github.com/SOsintOps/intelligence-field-notes) 0.1.2. The original is the reference; this copy is here for offline use.

How an open-source investigation is run, from the question to the archived capture: the OSINT cycle, the 5W1H method, collection discipline and operational security. The tools change every year; this part changes slowly.

## The OSINT Cycle
OSINT follows the [intelligence cycle](analytic-standards.md#the-intelligence-cycle) with stage names that fit open sources:
1.  **Planning:** objective, sources to try, legal boundaries, OPSEC level, time box. Write the question down in one sentence before the first search.
2.  **Collection:** search, capture and preserve. Manual observation and automated tools together.
3.  **Processing:** filter, normalise, translate, deduplicate, enrich; grade every item.
4.  **Analysis:** extract meaning, find patterns, test hypotheses against each other.
5.  **Production:** the report, shaped for its reader.
6.  **Feedback:** adjust to the reader's response and the new requirements.

## The 5W1H Analytical Method
The 5W1H method (Who, What, When, Where, Why, How) is a cognitive tool that imposes order on chaotic data, and a structured path from raw open-source information to finished intelligence. It is also a safeguard against confirmation bias and tunnel vision: a question you have not asked is a gap you have not seen. The UNODC manual asks the same six questions of every hypothesis.

### Who: Identifying Actors and Networks
All the individuals, companies and entities connected to the investigation, and beyond their names, the relationships, motivations and structures between them.
- **Guiding Question:** Who are the primary and secondary actors (individuals, groups, organisations)?
- **Guiding Question:** Who are the key nodes and influencers within the network?
- **Guiding Question:** Who provides financial, logistical or ideological support?

### What: Defining the Event and Assets
The core incident or activity, and the focus of the investigation.
- **Guiding Question:** What specific event or activity is under investigation?
- **Guiding Question:** What capabilities or TTPs (Tactics, Techniques and Procedures) were demonstrated?
- **Guiding Question:** What specific vulnerability was exploited?

### When: Establishing the Temporal Dimension
The timeline: events in chronological order, to reveal patterns, triggers and sequences.
- **Guiding Question:** What is the precise start and end date and time of the event?
- **Guiding Question:** What is the full timeline of significant actions?
- **Guiding Question:** Is there a pattern in time of day, day of week or season?

### Where: Pinpointing Location and Jurisdiction
Physical and digital locations, and the constraints they bring.
- **Guiding Question:** Where is the physical location (country, city, address, coordinates)?
- **Guiding Question:** Where is the digital location (website, IP address, platform, forum, channel)?
- **Guiding Question:** Which legal or administrative jurisdictions apply?

### Why: Assessing Intent and Motivation
Often the most important question and the hardest; essential for assessing threats and anticipating behaviour. Answers to "why" are almost always judgements, never observations: label them so.
- **Guiding Question:** What is the stated or inferred motive (financial, political, ideological, personal)?
- **Guiding Question:** Why this target, this timing, this method over the alternatives?
- **Guiding Question:** What is the root cause of the problem or event?

### How: Detailing the Modus Operandi
The operational mechanics: methods, tools and procedures.
- **Guiding Question:** How were the actions executed, step by step?
- **Guiding Question:** Which tools, software or hardware were used?
- **Guiding Question:** How was detection avoided or security circumvented?

## Collection Discipline
What separates an investigation from browsing is that every result can be found again, by you or by someone checking your work.
- **One case, one folder.** Everything collected for a case lives in one place, named consistently, never mixed with another case.
- **Capture, do not bookmark.** Pages change and disappear; platforms delete posts and accounts. Save the page (HTML or WARC), a full-page screenshot and, for media, the original file.
- **Record the context of every capture:** the URL, the date and time in UTC, the tool and its version, the account or persona used, and what you were looking for.
- **Hash on capture.** A SHA-256 of each file, recorded when it is saved, proves later that it has not changed.
- **Archive the public pages that matter** in a public archive as well (for example the Wayback Machine), when doing so does not tip off the subject.
- **Keep the dead ends.** A search that found nothing is information: it narrows the gap and stops the next analyst repeating it.
- **Separate the raw from the analysed.** Captures are never edited; notes, translations and annotations go alongside them.
- **Grade as you go.** Every item gets a source and an information grade when it enters the case (see [Source Evaluation](source-evaluation.md)), not at the end when memory has faded.

## Operational Security (OPSEC) Best Practices
OPSEC is not optional. It protects you, the investigation and the people around it from exposure and counter-intelligence. Conduct all activities ethically and within the law.
- **Identity Segregation:** never use personal accounts or equipment for investigations. Use dedicated, non-attributable accounts and personas, not linked to each other or to your real identity.
- **Secure Infrastructure:** use a trusted, no-log VPN while collecting. For sensitive work use a dedicated virtual machine, rebuilt or restored to a clean snapshot between cases. Consider the Tor Browser where the target is not hostile to Tor traffic.
- **Sterile Browsing Environment:** a dedicated browser with a separate profile per persona, privacy extensions (ad, script and tracker blocking), and cookies, cache and history cleared regularly.
- **Disciplined Online Conduct:** mind your footprint. Give no unnecessary personal information when registering, use unique strong passwords and addresses per persona, and remember that what a persona likes, shares or follows profiles it.
- **Passive before active:** prefer collection the subject cannot see. Viewing a profile, joining a group or sending a request may notify the subject; decide it deliberately, never by accident.
- **Know what your tools send:** online lookups, AI services and enrichment APIs receive the identifiers you submit. Switch them on only when the identifier may leave your machine; prefer local tools and models; remove personal data from text before sending it out.
- **Secure Data Handling:** keep case data on encrypted storage, back it up, and set a retention and destruction policy for what is no longer needed.

## Legal and Ethical Limits
Open source does not mean free of rules. Before collecting, know which data protection law applies to you and to the subject (in Europe, the GDPR), what the platforms' terms allow, and where the line between observing and intruding lies. Collect only what the requirement needs, protect the people who appear in your material incidentally, and never deceive or pressure a real person into giving information. The [Berkeley Protocol](https://humanrights.berkeley.edu/publications/berkeley-protocol-on-digital-open-source-investigations/) is the reference for investigations whose results may reach a court.

## Further Reading
- **"OSINT Techniques: Resources for Uncovering Online Information"** (11th edition, 2024) by Michael Bazzell and Jason Edison - The practical reference on search techniques, tools and the investigator's virtual machine. [IntelTechniques](https://inteltechniques.com/book1.html)
- **"Extreme Privacy: What It Takes to Disappear"** (5th edition, 2024) by Michael Bazzell - Digital security and anonymity, the background of every OPSEC rule above. [IntelTechniques](https://inteltechniques.com/book7.html)
- **"Deep Dive: Exploring the Real-World Value of Open Source Intelligence"** (Wiley, 2023) by Rae L. Baker - The intelligence cycle and OSINT across subjects, organisations, transport, infrastructure and finance, with case studies. [Wiley](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Deep+Dive%3A+Exploring+the+Real+world+Value+of+Open+Source+Intelligence-p-9781119933243)
- **"Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations"** (OHCHR and UC Berkeley Human Rights Center) - Collection, preservation and verification to evidential standard. [Human Rights Center](https://humanrights.berkeley.edu/publications/berkeley-protocol-on-digital-open-source-investigations/)
- **"Verification Handbook"** (European Journalism Centre) - Verifying user-generated content, images and accounts. [verificationhandbook.com](https://verificationhandbook.com/)
- **Bellingcat guides** - Step-by-step open-source investigation techniques. [bellingcat.com](https://www.bellingcat.com/category/resources/how-tos/)
